about: The launch across the harbour, played once at a set moment of the walk-through: the engines light 1 s into the stage's time, build for 5 s from the first ignition to release, and the rocket lifts straight off its pad and climbs, at Falcon Heavy's lift-off push against Earth's pull. It climbs straight up all the way (a launch seen from the shore shows no turn toward its aim within the minute). Frame: the scene record's (data/scene/launch.json).

motions.name: rocket_launch

sounds.name: rocket_launch
sounds.from: rocket_launch's own brief (data/sound/sounds.json, made by MOSS), faded in over the engines' 5 s from first ignition to release (the climb's lift)

motions.from: Falcon Heavy, whose night lift-off the effects are modelled on (data/effects/launch.json). Lift 5 s: SpaceX's Falcon Heavy Demonstration Mission press kit (February 2018), countdown: 'T-00:00:05 Engine controller commands side booster engine ignition sequence to start', 'T-00:00:03 ... center core ...', '00:00:00 Falcon Heavy liftoff'. Push 16.06 m/s/s: thrust at sea level 22,819 kN over mass 1,420,788 kg, both from SpaceX's Falcon Heavy page (spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-heavy, as archived by the Wayback Machine on 2021-01-03), held constant (the propellant burnt off in the climb is not modelled). Pull 9.81 m/s/s: the standard acceleration of gravity g_n = 9.80665 m/s/s (NIST CODATA), rounded. Start 1 s and length 59 s: SCORE's own timing of the walk-through. The rocket stands on its pad where the scene record lays it (data/scene/launch.json)
